correctness.rationale: For all r,h>0 and central planes, rotation reduces the geometry to z=kx. Polar integration gives A=r^2 sqrt(1+(ha/r)^2)I(a) with a=kr/h and exactly defined I. Substitution s=tan theta yields I(a)<2 arctan(1/a), while the cosine-product identity and coefficient inequalities show 2 arctan(1/a)<pi/sqrt(1+pi^2 a^2/4) for every a>0. Comparing h/r to pi/2 gives a strict inequality for all finite a>0. Endpoint areas pi r^2 and 2rh are direct disk/diamond geometry. Independent numerical polar/chord/closed-form checks pass for all tested parameters; these finite checks corroborate but do not establish the universal strict inequality.
